title: Spanish citizens first for housing
detail: Only Spanish citizens would get priority for protected and social housing (*vivienda protegida*) and for rent help. Rules that block "national priority" (*prioridad nacional*) would be changed or cancelled. The programme says strict border control must come before any housing policy.
c: Priority based only on nationality goes against art. 14 of the Constitution (equality), against EU law on long-term residents and against the ban on treating EU citizens differently. The regions decide who gets social housing. In our estimate, courts would cancel such rules.

title: Cancel the Housing Law and add tax breaks for long-term rentals
detail: Cancel the Housing Law (*Ley de Vivienda*). Give tax breaks for long-term rentals and tax deductions for Spanish tenants. Regulate tourist flats (*VUT*) and inspect illegal ones more. The programme gives no amounts for the deductions.
c: Cancelling the law is realistic together with PP. Deductions "for Spanish tenants" treat people differently by nationality, which EU tax law does not allow.
pos: Tax breaks give landlords a reason to keep renting long-term.
neg: Without rent limits, tenants in cities with high demand lose protection against rising rents. Part of the deductions ends up in higher rents.

title: Squatters out within 24 hours
detail: Remove squatters in under 24 hours and give the home back to the owner at once. Free legal help for victims. No taxes or bills for the owner while squatters live there. A stricter Criminal Code. Tenants who stop paying (*inquiocupación*) would be treated as fraud.
c: 24 hours does not fit with the protection of the home in the Constitution (art. 18.2) or with the right to a defence: there must be at least a short court process. If the squatter has not yet made the home their own, the police can already act at once.

title: Higher purchase tax for buyers from outside the EU and for funds
detail: A middle tax rate for purchases that bring more homes to long-term rental. A tax to put off buyers from outside the EU (*compradores no comunitarios*) and funds or companies that buy to make a quick profit. The money would pay for help for home buyers and protected housing. The programme gives no rates.
c: A tax on buyers from outside the EU is possible but legally risky: the EU rule on free movement of money (art. 63 TFEU) also covers buyers from outside the EU. A tax meant to stop funds from buying is hard to fit with the same rule.

s.t: Treaty on the Functioning of the EU, art. 63: free movement of capital (EUR-Lex)

title: *Autónomos*: no social security fee below the minimum wage
detail: A €0 social security fee (*cuota*) for self-employed people who earn less than the minimum wage (*SMI*). Above that, a fee from €50 that rises with income.
c: Similar to PP but wider: zero for everyone below the SMI. Social security would lose income, and employers would have a reason to use false self-employment. It can be done by law, but it is expensive.
pos: People on low incomes can start a business and leave work without contracts more easily.
neg: Lower fees mean smaller pensions later for the self-employed, a gap in social security money and a reason for "false self-employment".

title: Tax on money foreigners send abroad
detail: A tax on money that people send abroad (*remesas*), so that money earned in Spain helps the economy and services for people who live here. No rate is given.
c: A tax on money sent abroad goes against the EU rule on free movement of money and payments. The US brought in a similar 1% tax in 2026, but EU law does not apply to the US.

title: Cancel the 2021 labour reform
detail: Cancel the labour laws of the Sánchez government. The programme says they made jobs less secure, stopped employers from hiring and made the figures on temporary work look better than they are. It does not say what would replace them.
c: The 2021 reform can be cancelled by law. But it is linked to EU recovery money, and the share of temporary contracts fell from 25.4% (end of 2021) to 15.1% (end of 2025). Cancelling it would mean conflict with the EU and the unions.
pos: Employers get more freedom when they hire. Seasonal businesses would no longer need *fijos discontinuos* (permanent contracts for seasonal work).
neg: After the 2021 reform the share of temporary contracts fell (EPA: 25.4% at the end of 2021, 15.1% at the end of 2025). Critics say part of the fall is only a move to *fijos discontinuos*. Cancelling the reform would bring back more temporary contracts, plus conflict with the unions and with Spain's promises for NextGenerationEU money.

s.t: Labour Ministry: EPA analysis Q4 2025, temporary contracts 15.1%

title: End compulsory online appointments (*cita previa*)
detail: A right to be served in person at once at any state office, without booking an online appointment (*cita previa*) first.
c: PSOE makes the same promise. It is realistic in state offices, but it needs more staff.
pos: Older people and people without internet can use public services.
neg: Without more staff, the queues in offices get longer.

title: End *arraigo* and fast routes to citizenship
detail: End *arraigo* (residence based on your ties to Spain) to fight immigration without papers, and end the "fast routes" (*pasarelas rápidas*) to citizenship.
c: *Arraigo* is set in the immigration regulation (*Reglamento de Extranjería*), under the Immigration Law. A government can narrow it by royal decree. Ending it for good in the law needs an organic law (176 votes, together with PP). The result: more people without papers, working without contracts.
pos: It shows that entering without papers does not lead to legal status.
neg: Hundreds of thousands of people would stay without papers and work without contracts. The state gets less tax and fewer social security payments, workers are exploited more, and integration gets harder.

s.t: Real Decreto 1155/2024, the immigration regulation (Reglamento de Extranjería) (BOE)

title: Sending people back and "remigration"
detail: Send back people who live in Spain without papers (*repatriación*). Also "remigration" (*remigración*): a plan to help foreigners leave who, in the programme's words, do not contribute or live on benefits. The programme does not explain how.
c: Sending away large numbers of people without papers is not possible unless their countries agree to take them back. "Remigration" of legal residents because they receive benefits goes against EU rules and the European Convention on Human Rights.

title: One health card valid across Spain
detail: One health card (*tarjeta sanitaria única*) with one medical record for all of Spain. Not speaking a regional language should not stop anyone from getting a job in the health service.
c: One card is a long IT project with the regions. Dropping language requirements in public job exams would cause conflict with Catalonia, the Basque Country and Galicia, and courts have decided differently on this.
pos: Patients get care in any region, and doctors can see their medical history.
neg: It is a big IT project, and the language rule would cause conflict with Catalonia and the Basque Country.

title: End "health tourism"; no health care for people without papers
detail: End "health tourism" (*turismo sanitario*). People without papers would get no health care except in serious emergencies (*urgencia grave*). Check how much immigration costs the health service.
c: Excluding people without papers is possible by law (it happened from 2012 to 2018), but many regions kept treating them. In our estimate the savings are small, and health problems that are not urgent become urgent and more expensive.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 16/2012: restricted access to health care (BOE)
Real Decreto-ley 7/2018: universal access to the SNS restored (BOE)

title: Cut taxes on electricity
detail: A big cut in taxes on electricity for households, businesses and industry, an end to paying tax twice on it (*doble imposición*), and a national plan for energy independence. No rates are given.
c: Taxes on electricity can be cut (Spain did it from 2021 to 2023), but no rates are given. An EU rule sets minimum tax rates on energy.
pos: Cheaper electricity for households and industry.
neg: The state loses income that pays for the electricity system. Power companies may keep part of the saving.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 12/2021: suspension of the electricity generation tax (BOE)

title: Nuclear plan: keep plants open and build new ones
detail: Keep the current nuclear plants by cancelling the closing timetable (*calendario de cierre*). Study new reactors next to the current plants as soon as possible, and move good projects forward quickly.
c: Keeping plants open is realistic if the owners agree (see PP). In our estimate, new reactors take 10 to 15 years and cost billions (France's Flamanville plant was connected to the grid only in December 2024). Private companies will not build them without state guarantees.
pos: It keeps a stable supply of low-carbon electricity.
neg: New reactors are expensive and, in our estimate, take 10 to 15 years to build. Owners may not invest without state money.

s.t: EDF, 21 Dec 2024: Flamanville 3 reactor connected to the grid
